conventions: px = reference-image pixels, x right, y down, integer = pixel centre. Angles in image space: 0 deg = +x, positive = clockwise on screen. method 'measured' = computed from the masks/particles by scripts/reference_masks.py; 'read' = placed by eye on 4-8x zoomed crops. uncertainty_px is a 1-sigma-ish radius, not a hard bound.

thumb_tip.note: the thumb per decision D2 (the digit whose nail faces the viewer). Not a silhouette extreme (the ring finger emerges from behind the thumb's end): the core pixel (grey < 100) of the stroke that outlines the thumb's end and its nail, furthest along the thumb axis (45 deg, read from its two edges, 40-59 deg) inside the window [540, 440, 572, 468], which is read by eye. Inside that window the answer is stable: axis 30-60 deg moves it <= 5 px and the grey level 60-160 <= 3.6 px. The window itself is load-bearing -- widening it by 5-8 px picks up the next stroke down-right, which belongs to the ring finger, and the answer jumps 19.7-42.4 px (meta.json -> left.hand_read_choices.thumb_tip_sensitivity). The 8 px uncertainty is set by the reading convention, not by noise: this is the distal corner of the nail outline, while the user's D2 reading (548-559, 461) marks the lower-left of the same nail end, 4.2-14.3 px away; k=2 covers that range. (Until 2026-09-19 the stored value was (548,461).)

wrist.note: centre of the narrowest cross-section of the density silhouette between x 1150 and 1320 (measured perpendicular to the forearm axis). ACROSS the axis this is good to ~5 px; ALONG the axis it is poorly defined: the section width falls from ~187 px (x ~1080) to ~117 px by x ~1260 and then stays at 115-126 px until the particles thin out past x ~1320, so any point on that plateau is 'narrowest' within noise. Hence 35 px (the plateau's half-length). The anatomical wrist -- where the taper ends -- is at the proximal end of the plateau, x ~1250

wrist_axis_deg.note: line fit to the mid-points of the density silhouette's vertical extent for x 1150..1320 (before the cut); image space, 0 = +x, positive = down-right; points from hand to elbow

index_tip_gap_px.note: distance between left index_tip and right index_tip; the uncertainty is dominated by the particle tip (3 px)

silhouette_gap_px.note: closest approach of the two silhouettes

mask_tip_gap_px.note: distance between the two index tips measured on the silhouette masks with the tip rule; this is the gap a silhouette render is compared with
